recipes.title: Bolognese

ingredients.name: minced meat (beef, or a beef/pork mix)
ingredients.raw: 650 g minced meat (beef, or a beef/pork mix)

ingredients.name: parmesan rind (optional — or grated parmesan at the end/table instead)
ingredients.raw: parmesan rind (optional — or grated parmesan at the end/table instead)

instructions: Render the pancetta in a pot over medium-low heat until the fat has rendered out (don't let it go too crisp).
Add onions to the fat and cook until translucent.
Add carrots and celery, continue cooking the soffritto until softened.
Brown the mince separately in a different pan, in small batches, over medium-high heat — dry the meat first, don't crowd the pan, let it sit undisturbed to develop a crust.
Once all batches are browned, combine the meat with the vegetables in the pot.
Deglaze the empty meat pan with the coffee, scraping up the fond, then pour it into the pot with everything else.
Add the milk to the meat and vegetables, and let it simmer down for 5-10 minutes before adding tomato — this tenderizes the meat before the acid hits it.
Add tomato purée and let it fry/toast for a couple of minutes to lose its raw acidity and deepen in color.
Add beef stock, bay leaves, parmesan (rind if using — pull out before serving; grated parmesan goes in at the end or table instead), and your spices.
Bring to a gentle simmer (small occasional bubbles, not a boil).
Simmer partially covered for the bulk of the cook, removing the lid for the last 20-30 minutes if it needs to reduce further.
Total time 2-4 hours: stir every 20-30 minutes and scrape the bottom to prevent sticking. Add a splash of stock/water if it's reducing too fast.
Check doneness: the sauce should be thick enough to hold a clear trail when a spoon is dragged across the pot's bottom.
Taste and adjust seasoning at the very end, since balance shifts over the long simmer.
recipes.notes:
Servings and the coffee/milk amounts are for roughly this quantity of mince (650g) — coffee can run up to 3 tbsp and milk up to 200ml if you want to push it.

Since milk is in the sauce, fridge life drops to 3-4 days, not the usual week-to-week-and-a-half. Freeze portions if you want to keep it longer.

recipes.title: Chicken Curry Crumble

ingredients.name: sugar (less is better — 30g worked well)
ingredients.raw: 50 g sugar (less is better — 30g worked well)

instructions: Peel the apple. Cut it into small cubes along with the aubergine and tomatoes. Cut the chicken escalopes into strips.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the aubergine down.
After 10 minutes, add the chicken, tomato, and apple.
Sprinkle with curry powder and desiccated coconut. Season with salt and pepper. Cook for another 10 minutes.
At the end of cooking, add the coconut milk and stir.
Pour the mixture into a gratin dish.
In a bowl, make the crumble topping by rubbing the flour, soft butter, and sugar together with your fingertips until sandy in texture.
Crumble the topping over the mixture and sprinkle with curry powder and desiccated coconut.
Bake the crumble for 25 minutes in an oven preheated to 200°C (gas mark 6/7).

recipes.title: Lamb Couscous
instructions: In a large pot, brown the lamb shoulder in butter.
Add the onion. Season with salt and pepper. Cover with water.
Add the carrots, leeks, courgettes, aubergine, pepper, garlic, chopped tomatoes, tomato purée, and celery stick.
Cook for 3 to 4 hours.
Add the chickpeas 30 minutes before the end of cooking.
Serve with couscous (semolina).

recipes.title: Morbier and Pear Quiche
instructions: Make the quiche filling: whisk the eggs with the salt, pepper, and freshly grated nutmeg, then add the cream and mix well.
Preheat the oven to 210°C (gas mark 7).
Peel the pears. Bring the water, sugar, and lemon juice to the boil, then poach the whole pears in it over low heat for 1 hour.
Butter a deep-sided tin about 21cm in diameter. Roll out the pastry and line the tin.
Once the pears are poached, drain them, cut them into quarters, and remove the cores. Arrange them in a rosette on the pastry.
Remove the rind from the morbier and cut it into 1/2cm cubes. Place the cubes between the pears.
Wash and finely chop the mint, and scatter it over the cheese.
Pour in the quiche filling and adjust the seasoning.
Bake for 30 minutes. Serve hot.
recipes.notes: You can use tinned or jarred pears in syrup instead — in that case, skip poaching them.

recipes.title: Rum Baba
instructions: Bring all the base ingredients (eggs, butter, milk) to room temperature.
Dissolve the yeast in the milk, just lukewarm and sweetened.
In a warm bowl, put in the flour and make a well in the centre.
Add the salt and the beaten eggs.
Mix in, gradually adding the yeast.
Work in the melted, cooled butter.
Work the dough by hand for ten minutes — it should be quite soft and runny.
Cover the bowl with a floured cloth and leave to rise somewhere warm for at least two hours, until it doubles in size.
Gently knock the dough back down.
Put it into a well-buttered 25cm-diameter mould and leave to rest for an hour.
Once the mould is about three-quarters full, bake (gas mark 6.5, 25-30 min) until the cake is dry and golden.
Turn it out of the mould while still warm and douse it with hot rum syrup.
For the syrup: heat the water and sugar, then add the rum off the heat just before it boils.
Serve with whipped cream or pastry cream.
recipes.notes: Rum in the syrup can go up to 6 tablespoons if you want it stronger.

recipes.title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
While the pasta cooks, fry the guanciale in a cold pan over medium heat until crisp and golden.
Whisk the whole eggs, yolk, and pecorino together in a bowl with a generous amount of black pepper.
Drain the pasta, reserving a cup of pasta water, and add it straight into the guanciale pan off the heat.
Quickly stir in the egg mixture, adding splashes of pasta water until glossy and coating the pasta.
Serve immediately with extra pecorino and pepper.
recipes.notes: Never let the eggs hit direct heat or you'll end up with scrambled egg pasta. Off-heat and quick stirring is the whole trick.

comments.author: Elias
comments.text: This is now the only carbonara I make, guanciale really is worth tracking down.

comments.text: Used pancetta since I couldn't find guanciale, still great.

recipes.title: Thai Green Curry
instructions: Simmer half the coconut milk with the curry paste in a pan until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the chicken and cook through, stirring occasionally.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk, lime leaves, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Add the bell pepper and green beans, simmer until just tender.
Stir through the thai basil at the end and serve with jasmine rice.

comments.author: Elias
comments.text: Great with a squeeze of lime right before serving.

comments.author: Sam
comments.text: Adding extra fish sauce is non-negotiable in my house.
